title: Semantic segmentation
summary: Assign a class to every pixel using spatial features and contextual information.
why: Produces dense boundaries that a single class label or bounding box cannot represent.
interview: Trace U-Net skips and explain atrous convolution and output stride.
derivation: A U-Net encoder reduces resolution while increasing channels. Decoder upsampling restores resolution and concatenates same-scale encoder features. Those horizontal skips carry spatial detail across the bottleneck.
FCN replaces fully connected classification with dense prediction. DeepLabv3+ combines dilated features, ASPP at multiple rates, and a decoder for boundary refinement.

steps.note: Save intermediate maps for skip connections.
Dilation gathers context without further downsampling.

steps.transformation: 1x1 projection to K class logits per pixel

traps: Interpolation of label masks must preserve class IDs; use nearest neighbor.
Class imbalance can hide poor foreground quality behind high pixel accuracy.
Padding and odd dimensions can break skip concatenation.
tradeoff: High-resolution feature maps improve boundaries but consume activation memory.
code:
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

low = torch.randn(2, 64, 16, 16)
skip = torch.randn(2, 32, 32, 32)
up = F.interpolate(low, size=skip.shape[-2:], mode="bilinear", align_corners=False)
fused = torch.cat((up, skip), dim=1)
assert fused.shape == (2, 96, 32, 32)

explanations.title: One label per pixel: FCN and U-Net
paragraphs: Semantic segmentation produces logits [B,K,H,W], where K is the class count. Argmax across K yields one class ID per pixel. It does not identify separate instances of the same class.

FCN replaces classification-only dense layers with spatial predictions and upsamples low-resolution features. U-Net has an encoder, bottleneck, and decoder with same-scale encoder-to-decoder skip connections. Concatenation along channels preserves fine detail that a low-resolution bottleneck may lose.

For a stage with decoder [B,128,64,64] and encoder skip [B,64,64,64], concatenation creates [B,192,64,64]. Upsampling does not create missing evidence by itself. Crop, pad, or resize carefully if odd spatial dimensions make skip tensors disagree.
explanations.flow:
image -> encoder 1 -> encoder 2 -> bottleneck
          | skip         | skip         |
          +--> decoder 1 <- decoder 2 <--+
                  -> per-pixel class logits

explanations.title: Dilated convolution and DeepLabv3+
paragraphs: Dilation increases a kernel receptive field by spacing sample points. For a 3x3 kernel with dilation 2, effective width is 5 although there are still nine weights per input/output channel pair. It does not increase feature resolution by itself.

ASPP evaluates parallel branches at different dilation rates and may include image-level context. Their features are combined so a location receives context at several scales. DeepLabv3+ adds a decoder that mixes contextual features with lower-level spatial detail for boundary refinement.

Very large dilation rates on a small feature map can sample mostly padding. A small output stride preserves resolution at higher activation cost. Compare boundary quality, mIoU, and latency at the actual input size.

explanations.title: Train and evaluate dense outputs correctly
paragraphs: Multiclass cross-entropy accepts [B,K,H,W] raw logits and integer targets [B,H,W]. Ignore labels exclude unknown or padded pixels. Multilabel masks use a different target and loss contract, typically independent binary logits.

Class imbalance can make background-heavy pixel accuracy misleading. Inspect per-class IoU and Dice, and consider class weighting or overlap losses when justified. Report how empty classes and ignore regions are handled in the metric.

Apply geometric augmentations consistently to image and mask. Interpolate discrete label masks with nearest-neighbor sampling, not bilinear class-ID mixing. Split at patient, scene, or source level when neighboring images share content.
